findings.evidence: i8839 p. 2, a spouse's child's expenses are not qualified; p. 3, a U.S. child's 2025 expenses on a not-final adoption are credited the year after payment. s3.adoption_stepchild_if_final is read only by s3.adoption_if_any, which requires s3.adoption_final_if_adoption true; with a not-final adoption no refusal and no credit arise (fixture b1mutB.s3.adoption_not_final: s3.adoption_if_any false, line 7 $0), so 'treated as qualified' changes nothing.

i8839 p. 3, Domestic Adoption, 2024 payments credited in 2025. Asked by s3.adoption_earlier and s3.adoption_us under s3.adoption_any; a Yes refuses s3.line7 (fixture redesign.credits.refuse.adoption_earlier_us).
i8839 p. 3, employer payments excluded in the year of payment. scope.adoption_benefits (gated by s3.adoption_any) asks whether an employer paid or repaid any adoption costs and refuses the return.

i8839 p. 3, Line 1. The form's source asks "Did that adoption (or, if more than one, any of them) become final", but the interview asks "Was that adoption final by the end of 2025?"; a filer with one final and one pending adoption may answer for the pending one, No, and the final adoption's credit is not refused. Rare; low. Remedy: carry 'or any of them' into the question.

unruled:gate:s3.prior_other_forms#1.class: no gate defect; the design's accepted residuals; one wide
unruled:gate:s3.prior_other_forms#1.reason: A carryforward with no 2024 return is the design's BUG-0620 (8); Form 8582-CR beside 'a four-digit number' is BUG-0620 (4); a Yes for an unrelated form costs two questions.

findings.evidence: f8859 p. 1, Line 4; f8396 p. 2. A credit carried from 2023 or earlier by a filer with no 2024 return: the help says "If you did not file for 2024, answer No". The design's named residual BUG-0620 (8). Low.
The question's "a page headed 'Form' and a four-digit number" beside Form 8582-CR (a suffix). The follow-up s3.prior_forms names 8582-CR. Low; BUG-0620 (4).
A 2024 return with only Form 8962 or another unrelated form answers Yes and is asked s3.prior_amt and s3.prior_forms, both No; nothing is refused.

unruled:person.mw_business#1.class: no gate defect; the Schedule C clause changes where the payments appear, not the tax
unruled:person.mw_business#1.reason: Both findings concern the 'with this pay reported on a business schedule' clause. A No sends the 1099 payments to line 1d and back out on Schedule 1 line 8s, which nets to the same AGI and tax as the Schedule C route; presentation only.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 24, Line 1d, "If you are a sole proprietor in a business of providing home care services, see the Schedule C instructions for how to report these amounts"; i1040sc p. 6, Medicaid waiver payments: report the full 1099 amount on line 1 and the excludable amount as a Part V expense ('Notice 2014-7'). A home-care sole proprietor who answers No is not refused: person.line1d puts the 1099 amount on line 1d and person.line8s takes the same amount out on Schedule 1 line 8s (amb.2025.mw_all_nontaxable treats the payments as nontaxable), so AGI and tax match the Schedule C route, where the payments net to zero; the earned-income choice (person.mw_earned) is asked either way. Only the place of the entry differs.

The question follows person.mw_1099 ('How much of that was reported on a Form 1099-MISC or 1099-NEC?'), so 'this pay' is that 1099 amount. Either reading of the clause leads to a No or a refusal; a No gives the line 1d/8s entries described in finding 0, with no change of tax.

unruled:person.tips_gov#1.class: no gate defect; WIDE and a minor UNCLEAR that errs toward Yes
unruled:person.tips_gov#1.reason: A Yes refuses f4137 line 10 (refuses when person.tips_gov_if_rows); answering Yes for under-$20 government tips only over-refuses.

findings.evidence: f4137 p. 2, Line 10, 'If line 6 includes tips you received ... as a federal, state, or local government employee'. Under-$20 tips are taken out at line 5, so a filer whose only government tips were under $20 a month answers Yes and is refused at f4137 line 10 although line 10 would be right. Safe.

The question is asked only of a person with a Form 4137 employer row (person.tips_gov_if_rows reads person.f4137_filed), so 'these unreported tips' are the tips of those rows. Every reading the finding lists includes the line 6 tips, so the wider readings err toward Yes and a refusal.

unruled:gate:person.eligible_educator#1.class: no gate defect; the calendar-year reading of '900 hours' is a low wording residual
unruled:gate:person.eligible_educator#1.reason: The question restates the instructions' test, but its 'In 2025' opening and missing help let a filer count only 2025 hours for a school year that straddles the year end. Filed as one low wording entry.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 93, 'who worked in a school for at least 900 hours during a school year'. The interview asks 'In 2025, did you work in a school ... for at least 900 hours during a school year?' with no help, so a teacher who left in June 2025 (or started in August 2025) can count only the calendar-2025 hours and answer No; person.educator_expenses_if_educator is then zero (up to $300 lost).
As finding 0, for a teacher who started in the 2025-26 school year: the question does not say that the school year, not calendar 2025, measures the 900 hours.

unruled:gate:person.has_hsa#1.class: no gate defect; the narrow case is covered by the HSA listing question; the citation is filed
unruled:gate:person.has_hsa#1.reason: The HSA list question tells the filer to list an HSA 'even if nothing went in or out in 2025', so a dormant HSA with an old excess opens the gate. The gate's citation (Parts II and IX) is wrong and is filed; the line 48 help is consistent with line 42.

findings.evidence: The gate counts Forms 8889 listed through $f8889, whose question is 'Did you have a health savings account (HSA) in 2025, or get money from one?' with help 'Answer Yes even if nothing went in or out in 2025'. A person whose excess from an earlier year is still in the account had an HSA in 2025, lists it, and is asked person.x_hsa_prior_excess ('Before 2025, was more put into your HSA than the limit ..., with some of the extra still in the account at the start of 2025?'), whose Yes refuses through person.x_other (BUG-0313's fix).

f5329 p. 2, Part VII, 'or you had an amount on line 49 of your 2024 Form 5329'. person.has_hsa, person.x_hsa_prior_excess and its gate carry the shared x_* locator quoting Parts II and IX, which say nothing about HSAs. Citation only; no value changes.

f5329 line 42, 'Enter the excess contributions from line 48 of your 2024 Form 5329'. The help ('Answer Yes if your 2024 Form 5329 has an amount on line 48, or if you never reported the excess') names the line that carries the excess forward; a line 48 amount without a line 49 tax is the over-refusal BUG-0313 accepted. Errs toward Yes.

unruled:gate:person.ira_files_8606#1.class: no gate defect; prior-year basis with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the Form 1099-R
unruled:gate:person.ira_files_8606#1.reason: The three NARROW cases all have a 2025 traditional IRA Form 1099-R, where retirement.ira_basis refuses a filer with earlier nondeductible contributions; the SOURCE finding is the same split of the Who Must File conditions between the two places.

findings.evidence: Each traditional IRA Form 1099-R (distribution or conversion) asks retirement.ira_basis, 'Have you ever put money into a traditional IRA that you did not deduct on a tax return?' (help: 'If any of your earlier tax returns includes Form 8606, answer Yes. ... a Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses through retirement.special. The gate person.ira_files_8606 opens line 2 only for a 2025 nondeductible contribution; basis from earlier years with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the 1099-R. f8606 Part I, 'You took distributions from a traditional IRA in 2025 and you made nondeductible contributions ... in 2025 or an earlier year'.

Each traditional IRA Form 1099-R (distribution or conversion) asks retirement.ira_basis, 'Have you ever put money into a traditional IRA that you did not deduct on a tax return?' (help: 'If any of your earlier tax returns includes Form 8606, answer Yes. ... a Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses through retirement.special. The gate person.ira_files_8606 opens line 2 only for a 2025 nondeductible contribution; basis from earlier years with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the 1099-R. A partial Roth conversion is a 1099-R distribution from the traditional IRA, so the same question is asked.

Each traditional IRA Form 1099-R (distribution or conversion) asks retirement.ira_basis, 'Have you ever put money into a traditional IRA that you did not deduct on a tax return?' (help: 'If any of your earlier tax returns includes Form 8606, answer Yes. ... a Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses through retirement.special. The gate person.ira_files_8606 opens line 2 only for a 2025 nondeductible contribution; basis from earlier years with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the 1099-R. The repaid distribution is itself a 2025 Form 1099-R from a traditional IRA with basis; the basis question is asked on it. A qualified reservist repayment is refused through scope.reservist_repaid (ira.reservist_repaid).

The gate covers the 2025-contribution bullet of i8606 Who Must File; the bullets for distributions or conversions with earlier basis are handled by retirement.ira_basis on each 1099-R, as above. The line's citation names only the first bullet; no case drops.

unruled:gate:person.mw_has_1099#1.class: no gate defect; a home-care business without a Form 1099 gets the same tax through lines 1d and 8s
unruled:gate:person.mw_has_1099#1.reason: The business question matters only to where nontaxable payments appear; without a 1099 the tool's line 1d/8s treatment gives the same AGI, tax and earned-income choice as the Schedule C route.

findings.evidence: Without a Form 1099 the payments not in W-2 box 1 are person.mw_other: they go on line 1d only if the person chooses them as earned income (person.mw_other_1d) and are then excluded on Schedule 1 line 8s (person.line8s), or else stay out of income. i1040sc p. 6 nets excludable Medicaid waiver payments to zero on Schedule C ('report the nontaxable and excludable amount as an expense in Part V'). The tax and the earned-income choice are the same; only the form the amounts would appear on differs (amb.2025.mw_all_nontaxable).
Each person's Medicaid waiver questions are asked for that person (person collection), so the spouse with the business is in finding 0's situation for their own payments; same result.

unruled:gate:person.sav_trad_if_ira_owne.class: no gate defect; a contribution not yet made is not entered, and SEP/SIMPLE cases are WIDE
unruled:gate:person.sav_trad_if_ira_owne.reason: The interview counts 'Money put in by April 15, 2026 for 2025' and person.ira_owner counts 'one opened in early 2026 for 2025'; a filer who has not yet contributed enters the contribution when it is made.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 98, line 11, 'made, or that will be made by the due date'. person.ira_owner asks whether the person has an IRA 'now', with help 'one opened in early 2026 for 2025' counts, and person.sav_trad says 'Money put in by April 15, 2026 for 2025 counts'. A filer who has not opened or funded the IRA when filling in the return is outside what the questions can record; opening and funding it before filing answers both Yes. Not a gate defect.
SEP or SIMPLE money or a withdrawn contribution: the help says 'Do not count money that went into a SEP IRA or a SIMPLE IRA'; a Yes only leads to the amount question. Safe.

unruled:gate:person.simple_open_year#1.class: no gate defect; the 1963 to 1965 band is set by birth year, and the open years are the January 1 births
unruled:gate:person.simple_open_year#1.reason: person.simple_age puts anyone born 1963 to 1965 in the 60 to 63 band without a question; 1962 and 1966 are asked because a January 1 birth in those years attains 64 or 60 on December 31, 2025.

findings.evidence: person.simple_age: born from age.cut_64 (1962) up to the year before age.cut_60 (1966) goes to person.simple_age_60_63_years, which returns person.catchup_age60_63 whenever person.simple_open_year is false. Born 1963, 1964 or 1965 is in the 60 to 63 band ($5,250); the gate's otherwise value is read only for 1962 and 1966.

p560 p. 16, 'in a tax year in which they attain age 60, 61, 62, or 63'. Under the day-before rule the project applies (person.born_jan1's help), a person born January 1, 1962 attains 64 on December 31, 2025, and one born January 1, 1966 attains 60 that day; so the birth date does decide the band in those two years, as the gate says.
Everyone born in 1962 or 1966 is asked so that the January 1 births can be told apart; one question, no amount dropped.

unruled:gate:person.under16_open_year#1.class: no gate defect; a filer born 2011 or later is under 16 by birth year and refused
unruled:gate:person.under16_open_year#1.reason: person.under16 is true for anyone born after 2010 without a question; only 2010, where a January 1 birth is 16 on December 31, 2025, is asked. The age-16 refusal is the owner's entry check (amb.2025.filer_under_16).

findings.evidence: person.under16 is 'birth_year > age.cut_16 (2010)' or (born 2010 and person.under16_at_year_end_if_open_year). A filer born in 2011 or later is under 16 from the first branch and is refused (household.filer_under16); the open-year gate exists only for 2010.

amb.2025.filer_under_16: the text has no minimum filing age; the owner chose to refuse a filer or joint spouse under 16 at the end of 2025 as an entry check citing the Self-Select PIN sentence, without claiming the text forbids the return. The citation is the one sentence that names age 16, as recorded.

The refusal deliberately ignores first-time-filer status and the signing method (amb.2025.filer_under_16, owner's decision 2026-10-22); a filer born in 2010 who is under 16 is refused. Over-refusal by design.

unruled:gate:person.x_edu_account#1.class: no gate defect for the earlier Coverdell excess (the question asks whether an account was held at any time in 2025); the ABLE contributor case is a residual; citation filed
unruled:gate:person.x_edu_account#1.reason: The interview asks 'At any time in 2025, did you have a 529 plan, a Coverdell education savings account or an ABLE account, or was one held for you?', not about 2025 activity, so a dormant account with an old excess is asked the excess question. The line's label and source say 'money put into or taken out of', which misled the reviewer; filed with the citation.

findings.evidence: The interview question is about holding the account at any time in 2025; a beneficiary whose Coverdell still holds a 2024 excess answers Yes and is asked person.x_edu_excess ('Was more than the yearly limit put into a Coverdell education savings account or an ABLE account held for you, and is the extra still in the account?', help 'This includes an excess from an earlier year'), whose Yes refuses through person.x_other. The label/source mismatch is in BUG-0865.

i5329 Part VIII, net income on a returned ABLE excess 'is includible in the gross income of the contributor'. A parent who contributed to a child's ABLE account holds no account and answers No; the returned income is not asked anywhere else. Rare.
f5329 p. 3, Part IX (missed RMDs) is the locator of person.x_edu_account and its gated lines; the governing Parts II, V and VIII are not all cited. Citation only.
An account with only qualified distributions answers Yes and is asked two questions it answers No. Safe.

unruled:gate:dependent.other_only_spouse.class: no gate defect; a false gate sends the spouse's competing claim to the general tie-breaker refusal
unruled:gate:dependent.other_only_spouse.reason: The gate is household.mfs (f1040.status = mfs). When it is false, or when the answer is No, dependent.spouse_settles is false and dependent.tiebreak_unsettled takes dependent.tiebreak_spouse_or_other, then dependent.tiebreak_other, which refuses whenever dependent.other_claimant is Yes and the other person is a taxpayer or the child is also the filer's qualifying child. The spouse's claim is never treated as zero: it is refused. Only the case the tool computes (spouse the only other person, not claiming, filer a parent: p501 p. 17 Example 6; amb.2025.mfs_spouse_qc) depends on the gate.

findings.evidence: p501 p. 15 tie-breaker. Executed (fixture mfsl4.other_relative_too, married filing separately, other_claimant Yes, other_only_spouse No): other_only_spouse_if_mfs false, spouse_settles false, tiebreak_other true, and f1040.line19, dependent[kid].ctc_amount and line 27a refuse at dependent[kid].qc_tiebreak / eic_tiebreak ('The tie-breaker rules are outside this tool'). A third person who is also a claimant therefore gives a refusal, not a dropped spouse claim.

i1040gi p. 17, '(other than your spouse if filing jointly)'. On a head of household return the gate is false and the path is the same as finding 0: dependent.other_claimant (help: 'On a separate return, your husband or wife counts') Yes leads to dependent.qc_tiebreak, which refuses (executed path as finding 0). No computed claim drops the spouse.

i1040gi p. 17. The gated question asks facts ('Is your husband or wife the only relative, besides you, who lived with this child for more than half of 2025 and could claim them?'). A No (an unsure filer, or a third relative) refuses at qc_tiebreak (executed, finding 0). A Yes missing a third non-parent relative leads to the spouse question; with the filer a parent claiming the child, the parent wins against a non-parent (i1040gi p. 21, 'If only one of the persons is the child's parent'), so the result is unchanged.

unruled:gate:dependent.ptc_files#1.class: defect: the question states only the single under-65 non-blind limits
unruled:gate:dependent.ptc_files#1.reason: dependent.ptc_files decides whether the dependent's modified AGI enters f8962 line 2b (dependent.ptc_magi_counted). A married dependent is refused before this matters (dependent.married, 'A married dependent is outside this tool'), and Form 8814 is refused (f1040.line16 on scope.f8814). The combined test is in the help. The 65-or-older or blind dependent has no stated limit: BUG-0861.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 10, Chart B, married dependents ($5 rule). A dependent who has ever been married is asked dependent.married ('Was this person married at the end of 2025, or is this person on a joint tax return...? A Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses at dependent.married_screen_qc / married_if_ever_married_qr ('A married dependent is outside this tool'). The $5 rule never reaches a computed return.

i1040gi p. 10, Chart B combined test. The help shown with the question states it: 'A dependent with both kinds must also file when the two together are more than the larger of $1,350 and their pay (up to $15,300) plus $450.'

i8962 p. 8, Form 8814 amounts. Form 8814 is refused: scope.f8814 ('This is the choice made on Form 8814. A Yes ends the interview here') feeds the refusal on f1040.line16 (scope.other_line16, 'Forms 8814, 4972, 8615...'). No computed return has a Form 8814 child.

i1040gi p. 10, Chart B: 'Your unearned income was over $3,350' for a dependent 65 or older or blind. The help says 'These limits are for a single dependent under 65 who is not blind' and gives no other limit; a filer applying the stated $1,350 answers Yes and the modified AGI is counted on line 2b though the dependent need not file (PTC understated). Not a refusal.

unruled:gate:household.married#1.class: no gate defect; one low wording residual on common-law marriage
unruled:gate:household.married#1.reason: The gate household.married is household.marriage_possible (status mfj, mfs or qss, or household.ever_married for single and head of household) and then household.married_dec31. The interlocutory decree is stated in the help. The common-law marriage is stated in the gate's help (household.ever_married: 'Count a marriage that has ended, and a common-law marriage') but not in married_dec31's help: BUG-0863. The WIDE is accepted.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 14 / p501 p. 6, interlocutory decree. household.married_dec31 help: 'A divorce that was not yet final on December 31 means you were still married'.

p501 p. 6, Considered married 2 (common-law marriage). The gate question household.ever_married says 'Count ... a common-law marriage', so the possibility is reached; the gated question 'Were you married on December 31, 2025?' and its help do not repeat it (the line source does, from BUG-0280). A filer who answers the two inconsistently skips household.considered_unmarried and keeps head of household.

p501 p. 6. Joint filers and legally separated filers who reach the question answer it; a Yes asks the considered-unmarried question, which costs a question only (household.filing_status_conflict and hoh tests read it). No amount dropped.

unruled:gate:household.mfs#1.class: no gate defect; the head of household lived-apart test is a separate question
unruled:gate:household.mfs#1.reason: household.mfs_living_if_mfs feeds only married-filing-separately tests: household.mfs_apart_all_year (ssb worksheet line 8, line 6d, ira, s1, person) and household.mfs_apart_last6 (eic.mfs_same_home, f2441 line A). The head of household test for a married filer who lived apart is household.considered_unmarried ('You lived apart from your husband or wife for the last six months of 2025, you paid more than half the cost of your home, ...'), gated by household.married, not by this gate, and filing status is an input, so there is no circularity.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 15, Married persons who live apart. The head of household test reads household.considered_unmarried_if_married (asked of anyone married on December 31), not household.mfs_living. Every consumer of household.mfs_living_if_mfs is an MFS-only rule (grep forms/2025: ssb.yaml, eic.yaml eic.mfs_same_home, f2441.yaml line A, ira.yaml, s1.yaml, person.yaml), where together_late is the right default off MFS.

i1040gi p. 31, Line 6d. Every MFS filer is asked when they lived with the spouse; it also feeds eic.mfs_same_home and f2441 line A, so it is not idle without benefits. One question, no amount dropped.

unruled:gate:f1040.digital_assets#1.class: defect: the gate help treats a holder credited with staking or fork coins as a No (BUG-0896)
unruled:gate:f1040.digital_assets#1.reason: The page-1 question itself is the IRS question; its help's Yes examples omit rewards credited while holding.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 16, 'Received new digital assets as a result of mining, staking, and similar activities', 'Received digital assets as a result of a hard fork'. The help of f1040.digital_assets says 'Buying crypto with dollars and holding it ... is a No' and names only being paid, swapping and spending as Yes, so a passive staker or fork recipient can answer No and s1.digital_income_if_assets (line 8v) is not asked.

f1040.digital_assets is the Form 1040 page-1 digital asset question, which must be answered for any disposal; the extra cost to a seller is one question (s1.digital_income, whose help says sales are asked with sales).

unruled:gate:f1040.estimated_any#1.class: defect: amended-return overpayment and joint payments sent by a former spouse are outside the gate wording (BUG-0897)
unruled:gate:f1040.estimated_any#1.reason: i1040gi p. 39 includes an overpayment applied from an amended return and joint payments with a former spouse; the gate names only payments sent and a 2024 refund applied.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 39, 'Include any overpayment that you applied to your 2025 estimated tax from your 2024 return or an amended return.' f1040.estimated_any names only 'a 2024 refund applied to your 2025 tax'.

i1040gi p. 39, 'If you got divorced in 2025 and you made joint estimated tax payments with your former spouse'. The gate's spouse clause is 'on a joint return' and the help says payments 'you send yourself'.
Form 1040 line 26 says 'amount applied from 2024 return'; the gate calls it 'a 2024 refund applied', which a filer who received no check may not recognize. Low part of BUG-0897.

unruled:gate:f1040.withheld_other_any#1.class: defect (low): the help does not name Forms 8805 and 8288-A (BUG-0898)
unruled:gate:f1040.withheld_other_any#1.reason: The gated question f1040.line25c_other names both forms, but the gate's help lists only Form 1099, W-2G, SSA-1099, RRB-1099, Schedule K-1 and Form 1042-S.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 39, Line 25c, 'Tax withheld that is shown on Form 1042-S, Form 8805, or Form 8288-A.' Form 8805 tax is paid without a payment to the partner; 'taken out of money paid to you' and a help without Form 8805 permit a No. 'If you are not sure, answer Yes' mitigates; low.
Form 8288-A (FIRPTA) and K-1 withholding: K-1 is named in the help ('Tax withheld on a Schedule K-1 ... counts too'); Form 8288-A is not. Same low entry.

unruled:gate:rec.has_mortgage_if_path#1.class: no gate defect; a form pointer and the spouse reading
unruled:gate:rec.has_mortgage_if_path#1.reason: rec.has_mortgage asks 'a refund or credit of home mortgage interest you deducted for 2024 (box 4 of Form 1098)'.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 24, 'the amount should be shown in box 4 of Form 1098'. The parenthetical is a pointer to where the amount usually appears; the question's test is 'a refund or credit of home mortgage interest you deducted'. Low.
'Was any of it' refers to scope.recovery, which asks about money paid back to 'you (or, on a joint return, your spouse)'.

unruled:gate:rec.has_other_if_path#1.class: no gate defect; earlier years and sales tax are refused, reimbursements are named
unruled:gate:rec.has_other_if_path#1.reason: rec.has_other asks 'a refund or reimbursement of something else you deducted on your 2024 Schedule A ... such as a casualty loss reimbursed'.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 27, separate worksheet per year. rec.not_2024 ('Was any of the money paid back in 2025 for something paid or deducted before 2024?', help 'For example a 2023 casualty loss reimbursed in 2025. A Yes ends the interview here') is asked after any Yes to scope.recovery (rec.not_2024_if_any), whatever the 2024 itemizing answer, and refuses.

p525 p. 27 footnote 2, sales tax refunds. rec.sales_tax ('Was any of the money paid back a refund of sales tax?', 'A Yes ends the interview here') is asked after any Yes to scope.recovery and refuses; p525 p. 27 footnote 2 is therefore never computed.
The question says 'a refund or reimbursement', with 'a casualty loss reimbursed' as its example.

unruled:gate:rec.has_property_tax_if_pat.class: no gate defect; the question asks about tax deducted for 2024
unruled:gate:rec.has_property_tax_if_pat.reason: rec.has_property_tax asks 'a refund of state or local real estate tax or personal property tax you deducted for 2024'.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 26, Worksheet 2a line 4 (taxes paid in 2024). The question's test is tax 'you deducted for 2024', which is tax paid in 2024 whatever period the bill covered; a bill paid before 2024 is refused by rec.not_2024.

unruled:gate:rec.joint_any#1.class: no gate defect; state income tax refunds take the refund path, which has its own separate-returns question
unruled:gate:rec.joint_any#1.reason: rec.joint_any = scope.recovery and a joint 2025 return.

findings.evidence: A state or local income tax refund is asked on the refund path: on a joint return refund.two_returns asks whether the refunds were of both spouses' tax on separate 2024 returns, and refund.two_itemized refuses when either itemized ('A Yes is outside what this tool prepares').

scope.recovery asks about an amount 'whose deduction or credit on an earlier year's return lowered your tax'; its help says a 2024 standard-deduction filer answers No for itemized items. An itemizer will ordinarily take a deducted item as having lowered the tax, and Worksheet 2 then computes the part. A filer who judges the deduction made no difference is a low residual.

unruled:gate:rec.path#1.class: defect: the joint-return whose-return case (BUG-0899); the rest residual or accepted WIDE

findings.evidence: p525 p. 25. On a joint return with separate 2024 returns where only the spouse itemized, refund.itemized ('Did you itemize ...') gets a truthful No.

scope.recovery asks about an amount 'whose deduction or credit on an earlier year's return lowered your tax'; its help says a 2024 standard-deduction filer answers No for itemized items. An itemizer will ordinarily take a deducted item as having lowered the tax, and Worksheet 2 then computes the part. A filer who judges the deduction made no difference is a low residual.

scope.recovery says 'paid back an amount' with examples 'a refund of property tax, mortgage interest refunded (Form 1098 box 4), or a medical bill repaid by insurance'; rec.has_mortgage names 'a refund or credit'. A credit applied to a later bill or escrow is a low residual of the word 'paid back'.
Recoveries of other years and of nonitemized deductions open the gate, but rec.not_2024 and rec.nonitemized then refuse them; the cost is the questions asked.

unruled:gate:refund.worksheet#1.reason: refund.worksheet is refund.worksheet_one unless refund.two_returns; refund.two_itemized refuses the both-returns case.

findings.evidence: refund.two_returns' help: 'If only one of you got a refund, answer No; the questions that follow are then about that person's own 2024 return.'

The both-spouses case is not dropped: refund.two_itemized ('Did either of you itemize ...') refuses with 'The Form 1040 worksheet tests a refund against one 2024 return, so a Yes is outside what this tool prepares'; the i1040gi p. 88 exceptions are encoded in refund.not_prior_year, refund.exc_tax and refund.exc_who.
A refund for another year is refused by refund.other_year before the worksheet amount matters; the extra cost is the question.

unruled:gate:s2.amt_pab_ask#1.class: no gate defect; fund private activity bond dividends are refused through Form 1099-DIV box 13
unruled:gate:s2.amt_pab_ask#1.reason: div.box13 is asked with the less common 1099-DIV boxes and div.amt refuses any amount.

findings.evidence: i6251 p. 4, box 13 of Form 1099-DIV. div.box13 (asked when div.other_boxes is Yes; its help says most forms show amounts only in boxes 1a, 1b, 2a, 5, 7 and 12) and div.amt refuse any box 13 amount ('Review private activity bond interest for the alternative minimum tax; Form 6251 is outside scope'), independently of this gate.
Tax-exempt interest that is not from private activity bonds: the gate costs one question, answered zero.

unruled:gate:s2.options_any#1.class: no gate defect; line 8k is gated by the outer question itself
unruled:gate:s2.options_any#1.reason: s1.stock_options_if_options and s2.iso_if_options both guard on s2.options_any (forms/2025/s1.yaml, s2.yaml); its line source says 'exercise stock options from an employer' while the interview prompt adds 'or sell shares bought that way'.

findings.evidence: A non-employee director's or contractor's options: rare, and director fees are refused by person.se_screen; low.

There is no inner exercise helper: s1.stock_options_if_options chooses on s2.options_any, the gate itself, so a filer who sold ISO or ESPP shares answers Yes and s1.stock_options is asked ('For example when shares from an incentive stock option or a purchase plan were sold early').
A cashless exercise is caught by 'use stock options ... to buy shares, or sell shares bought that way'; low.
A sale of shares from options already taxed costs the gated questions only.

unruled:gate:scope.artist_official_if_w2.class: no gate defect; a fee-basis official without a W-2 is refused through the pay or self-employment screens
unruled:gate:scope.artist_official_if_w2.reason: Fees not on a W-2 are either wages without a form (scope.wages_no_form_if_pay, scope.other_income) or self-employment fees named by person.se_screen.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 93, Line 12. Fees with no W-2 are 'wages ... that are not on a W-2' (scope.pay_no_w2, then scope.wages_no_form_if_pay, refused by scope.other_income) or fees 'as a ... fee-basis government employee' on person.se_screen, refused by person.se_screened.
A performer who does not qualify answers Yes and is asked one more question, which they can answer No.

unruled:gate:scope.business_before#1.class: no gate defect; a 2025 interest is handled by its own K-1 entry
unruled:gate:scope.business_before#1.reason: scope.business_before gates the earlier-year screens (section 179 carryover, Form 8986, passive carryovers).

findings.evidence: i8582 p. 1. A partnership or S corporation interest held in 2025 is a k1p or k1s entry, whose own participation questions (k1p and k1s each carry the material participation tests) and Form 8582 (f8582) decide passive treatment; scope.passive is the screen for earlier-year carryovers and dispositions of businesses not otherwise entered ('Count a loss held back in an earlier year').
The before-2025 condition matches what the gated lines are for: carryovers and audit adjustments from earlier years. Current-year passive deductions are computed on the k1p/k1s entries and f8582.
'own a business' includes a sole proprietorship in plain words; a former freelancer who disallowed section 179 under the income limit is a low residual.

unruled:gate:scope.foreign_shares#1.class: defect: options or warrants, foreign ETFs and foreign-incorporated U.S.-listed stock (BUG-0905)
unruled:gate:scope.foreign_shares#1.reason: PFIC and CFC questions follow a Yes; the gate's wording leaves out several common PFIC holdings.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 114, Line 17p; an option on PFIC stock is treated as stock for section 1291. The gate asks only about owning 'shares'.
'other than through a U.S. mutual fund or ETF' can be read as excluding every ETF, including foreign-domiciled ones.
ADRs and U.S.-listed stock of a company incorporated abroad are not named.
A small holding in a large foreign operating company answers Yes and then No to the CFC and PFIC questions; the cost is two questions.

unruled:gate:scope.has_w2#1.class: no gate defect; the no-W-2 cases are refused by other screens
unruled:gate:scope.has_w2#1.reason: The gated questions read W-2 boxes; the same items without a W-2 reach other screens.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8t, ties the amount to box 11 of Form W-2 ('If you received such amount but box 11 is blank, contact your employer'); a nonqualified plan payment on a Form 1099 is a low residual.
Box 11 blank with the amount in box 1: the IRS text sends the filer to the employer; low.

Unreported tips: scope.tips_unreported ('cash or card tips at a job that were not reported in full to the employer, or tips that were not money'), asked after scope.pay_no_w2, whose help names 'tips not reported in full to your employer'.

409A income on Form 1099-MISC box 15: s2.other_tax ('For example the 20% tax on deferred pay that broke the rules or on a golden parachute payment', 'a Yes ends the interview here') is asked on every return.
Excess parachute payment on Form 1099-NEC: s2.other_tax names 'a golden parachute payment'.
Fees with no W-2: scope.wages_no_form_if_pay (scope.other_income) or person.se_screen ('fees as ... a fee-basis government employee') refuses.
Solo 401(k) deferrals: person.plan_screen ('money put in for yourself to another plan of your business too, such as a solo 401(k)', 'A Yes is outside what this tool prepares') refuses.
A SIMPLE-only participant over $16,500: the question says '$23,500 for most people'; a single SIMPLE employer caps deferrals at the plan limit, so only several SIMPLE plans can exceed it. Low.
Every return with a W-2 is asked these questions; the cost is the questions.

unruled:gate:scope.household_pay_if_pay#.class: defect (low): a driver or groundskeeper reads as a No (BUG-0903)
unruled:gate:scope.household_pay_if_pay#.reason: scope.pay_no_w2's help names 'pay for work in someone's home'.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 24, Line 1b. scope.household_pay asks about 'work in someone else's home'; a private driver is not named (a gardener is named in the help).
scope.pay_no_w2's help gives 'pay for work in someone's home' as its first example, so informal household pay is put to the filer before the household question.
A self-employed cleaner answers Yes; person.household_wages asks for household pay, and the cost is a question.

unruled:gate:scope.medicaid_waiver#1.class: defect: pay through an agency or fiscal agent, and the present tense (BUG-0904)
unruled:gate:scope.medicaid_waiver#1.reason: The gate asks whether a state Medicaid program paid the filer.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8s. Waiver pay usually comes through an agency or fiscal intermediary that issues the W-2.
'who lives in your home' in the present tense; low part of the same entry.

unruled:gate:scope.nol#1.class: defect: help limits the carried loss (BUG-0907)
unruled:gate:scope.nol#1.reason: scope.nol gates the carryover amount and the excess-business-loss refusal.

findings.evidence: i172 p. 4, a disallowed excess business loss is an NOL carryover; the help's 'A loss bigger than that year's income' excludes it when total income stayed positive.
A first-year 2024 NOL and a rental-sourced NOL: the help's 'carried forward on an earlier return' and its sources (business, disaster or theft).

unruled:gate:scope.recovery#1.class: defect (low): the help ties the standard-deduction test to 2024 (BUG-0908); other findings covered or residual
unruled:gate:scope.recovery#1.reason: scope.recovery gates rec.nonitemized, rec.not_2024 and rec.sales_tax.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 24, the test is the year of the deduction; the help says 'If you took the standard deduction for 2024 ... answer No', so a 2023 itemizer answers No and rec.not_2024's refusal is skipped.
A state income tax refund for 2023 is on the refund path: refund.other_year ('Was any of that refund for a year other than 2024?') refuses it.
A deduction that only increased a carryover: p525 p. 24's tax benefit rule; rare; low.
A downward price adjustment on a credited item: rare; low (BUG-0908 adds a credit example).
scope.recovery's 'lowered your tax' asks a judgment Worksheet 2 also makes; an itemizer ordinarily takes a deducted item as having lowered tax; low.

unruled:gate:scope.religious_work#1.class: defect (low): members of a religious order are not named (BUG-0909)
unruled:gate:scope.religious_work#1.reason: scope.clergy names order members; the gate does not.

findings.evidence: i1040sse p. 1, 'member of a religious order who hasn't taken a vow of poverty'; the gate names a church payer or clergy only.
A church employee with withholding answers Yes and No to the two gated questions; the cost is the questions.

unruled:gate:scope.rental#1.class: defect (low): 'anything you own' misses a leased item sublet (BUG-0910)
unruled:gate:scope.rental#1.reason: scope.rental gates the personal-property rental refusal.

findings.evidence: i1040se p. 5, rental of personal property is not limited to owned property.
Royalty-only or real estate-only filers answer one extra question.

unruled:gate:scope.strike_pay_if_pay#1.class: defect: lockout benefits and non-union strike funds (BUG-0906)
unruled:gate:scope.strike_pay_if_pay#1.reason: The parent names 'strike benefits'; the child says 'from a union'.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 24, Line 1h, 'Strike or lockout benefits'.
'from a union' in scope.strike_pay and person.strike.
Strike benefits on a Form 1099: the parent names 'strike benefits that are not on a W-2'; low.
'was a parent of yours alive' includes a stepparent or adoptive parent in ordinary use; low.
Nontaxable income counted: one extra question.
Age-convention edges: one extra question.
Filing requirement not tested: the gated question's help says Form 8615 applies only to a person who has to file.

unruled:rec.nonitemized#1.reason: rec.nonitemized refuses a recovery of a nonitemized deduction or a credit.

findings.evidence: The help's examples, 'a bad debt repaid after you deducted it, a business expense refunded', are deductions taken in figuring AGI, so 'without itemizing' is read as the type of deduction.
A price adjustment on a credited item that is not cash: rare; low.
A same-year reimbursement answered Yes: scope.recovery asks about a deduction 'on an earlier year's return'; the cost is a refusal in a rare misreading.
A credit recovery is refused although line 8z is unaffected: the tax increase on the credit is not computed, so the refusal is correct for the return.

unruled:rec.before_prior_year#1.reason: rec.not_2024 refuses recoveries for something paid or deducted before 2024.

findings.evidence: A 2024 nonitemized recovery is refused by rec.nonitemized ('a deduction taken without itemizing ... A Yes ends the interview here').
A 2023 bill with no tax benefit: a refusal where the amount would be zero; rare.
A credit or offset of a pre-2024 deduction: low.

unruled:rec.sales_tax#1.reason: rec.sales_tax refuses any sales tax refund.

findings.evidence: A sales tax refund that was never deducted is refused although it is not income; rare; the cost is a refusal.
'general sales tax' on a vehicle or lodging tax: low.

unruled:rec.two_returns#1.class: defect: a state refund of the other spouse's separate 2024 return is not counted (BUG-0899, extended)
unruled:rec.two_returns#1.reason: rec.two_returns' help 'Answer No if only one of you got money back' does not count the other spouse's state income tax refund.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 27, a separate Worksheet 2 per return. One spouse's recovery and the other spouse's state refund, each of their own separate 2024 return, are figured on one Worksheet 2 against one return (refund.taxable takes Worksheet 2 when other recoveries exist).

unruled:s1.gambling_pro#1.class: defect: the asked wording 'the way a living is made' is narrower than a trade or business of gambling
unruled:s1.gambling_pro#1.reason: Finding 0 covered: s1.gambling_winnings help names fantasy sports and sports bets, so the filer already counts fantasy winnings as gambling before this screen. Finding 1: the reviewer saw the form-line source ('in the trade or business of gambling (a professional gambler)'), but the interview asks 'Is gambling your (or, on a joint return, your spouse's) business, the way a living is made?', which a part-time business gambler with a job truthfully answers No; the winnings then stay on line 8b with no Schedule C or SE tax. Low.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 33: 'Winnings from fantasy sports leagues are gambling winnings.' The screen is reached only after s1.gambling_winnings, whose help lists 'lotteries, raffles, sports bets, fantasy sports'; a fantasy player has already entered the winnings as gambling and reads 'Is gambling your business' about that activity.

p525 p. 33: 'Engaging in gambling activities as a trade or business is considered self-employment. If you're in the trade or business of gambling, use Schedule C.' The interview prompt 'Is gambling your ... business, the way a living is made?' reads as the filer's livelihood; a regular, continuous side business answers No and line 8b takes Schedule C income. Low.

unruled:s1.nol_before_limit_date#1.class: no screen defect; the 80% limit is refused at Form 1040 line 15
unruled:s1.nol_before_limit_date#1.reason: Finding 0 covered: s1.nol_limit (forms/2025/s1.yaml; refusal on f1040.line15, 'Form 172, NOL deduction limitation (the 80% limit)') refuses whenever the carried loss is more than four times taxable income after deducting it, i.e. whenever the 80% cap could bind. Finding 1 covered by the amount question's help.

findings.evidence: i172 p. 1, NOL deduction limitation, '(b) 80% of the excess (if any) of taxable income computed without regard to deductions for NOLs, or QBI'. s1.nol_limit_test is s1.nol_amount_if_nol > 4 x (f1040.line11b - f1040.line14); f1040.line15 refuses on s1.nol_limit ('the limit of 80% of taxable income figured without the deduction may apply'). A post-2017-only filer above the cap is refused, not over-deducted.

i172 p. 1, Step 5. s1.nol_amount asks 'How much of that loss is still unused and carried into 2025?' with help 'Give what is still unused, after what earlier returns used'; that unused carryover is the deduction when the cap does not bind, and s1.nol_limit refuses when it may.

unruled:gate:s1.alimony_any#1.class: defect (low): the gate's definition 'support paid to a husband or wife' leaves out payments made for the spouse to a third party
unruled:gate:s1.alimony_any#1.reason: Finding 0: i1040gi p. 95 says 'payments to or for your spouse'; the gate's 'support paid to a husband or wife' invites a No from a payer whose decree sends the payments to a landlord or lender (same as false-no finding 0). Low. Findings 1 and 2 accepted WIDE (one follow-up question resolves them).

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 95, Line 19a: 'If you made payments to or for your spouse or former spouse under a divorce or separation agreement entered into on or before December 31, 2018'. Gate wording: 'pay or receive alimony: support paid to a husband or wife after a divorce or separation?'; the help names only child support and property division as exclusions. Low.
i1040gi p. 89, Line 2a. Post-2018 agreements pass the gate; s1.alimony ('made in 2018 or earlier?') answers No and nothing more is asked.
p504 p. 16, the 3-year recapture period. The 2023 start is needed for a 2025 recapture; extra filers answer one more question.

unruled:gate:s1.has_gambling#1.class: defect (low) on finding 3 only: s1.gambling_pro's 'the way a living is made'; the gate itself is sound
unruled:gate:s1.has_gambling#1.reason: Findings 0 to 2 are model errors: the reviewer saw only the helper's label tied to line 8b, but the asked question s1.gambling_winnings has no business exclusion and names the spouse. Finding 3 is the same wording defect as s1.gambling_pro#1 finding 1.

findings.evidence: The gambling winnings question s1.gambling_winnings asks 'How much did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) win from gambling in 2025, before subtracting any losses?' with help naming W-2G box 1, lotteries, raffles, sports bets and fantasy sports; it has no trade-or-business exclusion, so a professional's winnings are entered and s1.has_gambling holds.

s1.winnings_any asks 'did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) win money or a prize: from gambling, a lottery, a raffle, a contest or an award?'; a professional gambler did win money from gambling and answers Yes; nothing in the wording excludes business winnings.
s1.gambling_winnings asks 'How much did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) win from gambling in 2025'; the spouse's winnings are asked.

p525 p. 33, 'If you're in the trade or business of gambling, use Schedule C.' s1.gambling_pro asks 'Is gambling your ... business, the way a living is made?'; a part-time business gambler answers No. Low.

unruled:gate:s1.nol_separate#1.class: no gate defect; the remarried joint filer is caught by the joint branch
unruled:gate:s1.nol_separate#1.reason: Finding 0 is a model error: on an mfj return s1.nol_joint holds and asks s1.nol_not_married ('Were you and your spouse not married to each other in the year any of the loss arose, or in any year from then to 2025?'), whose Yes refuses through s1.nol_marital. Finding 1 accepted WIDE.

findings.evidence: i172 p. 3, Change in Marital Status, 'If you file a joint return, the NOL deduction is limited to the income of that spouse.' s1.nol_joint = scope.nol and status mfj gates s1.nol_not_married; a filer remarried since the loss year answers Yes (tick 'You two were not married to each other when it arose') and s1.line8a refuses on s1.nol_marital.
i172 p. 3, Joint to separate returns. A single or HOH filer with no joint history is asked one question and answers No.

unruled:gate:s1.winnings_any#1.class: defect: the gate asks what was won in 2025, not what was received, so lottery installments and sales of lottery rights are missed
unruled:gate:s1.winnings_any#1.reason: Findings 0, 1 and 3: s1.winnings_any is keyed to winning in 2025 ('In 2025, did you ... win money or a prize'), while lines 8b and 8i take amounts received in 2025: an installment of an earlier lottery win, a lump sum for selling future lottery payments, and a prize won in late 2024 and received in 2025 are truthful Noes, and line 8b or 8i drops them. Finding 2 (prize points) is in the same fix. Medium. Finding 4 accepted WIDE.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 33, Installment payments: 'you must include in your gross income the annual payments and any amounts you receive designated as interest on the unpaid installments'. Gate: 'In 2025, did you ... win money or a prize'. A 2025 installment on a 2015 win is a truthful No; s1.gambling_winnings_if_winnings (line 8b) is zero. Medium.
i1040gi p. 91, Line 8b: 'Gambling winnings include ... a lump-sum payment from the sale of a right to receive future lottery payments'. A sale is not a 2025 win; truthful No drops line 8b.

p525 p. 35, Prize points: 'taxable in the year they're paid or made available to you'. The gated s1.prizes help says 'Count prize points when you can use them', but the gate's help ('Count small winnings, winnings with no tax form, and prizes in goods') does not; a salesperson may answer No. Low part of the same fix.
p525 p. 35, Prizes and awards. The gate is keyed to the year of the win, income to the year of receipt; the fix asks about receipt.
p525 p. 35; i1040sc p. 6, Line 6. s1.prizes help leaves out pay from an employer, a business prize and a refused prize, and s1.gambling_pro refuses a professional; one or two extra questions.

unruled:gate:s1.has_sc#1.class: low defect: the look-back question misses a contract adjusted (not finished) in 2025; the rest is out of scope or accepted
unruled:gate:s1.has_sc#1.reason: The gate counts Schedules C. Every pass-through or farm case the reviewer raises ends the interview earlier: scope.k1 (partnership, S corporation, estate or trust; 'A Yes ends the interview here'), scope.farm (help: 'Count a farm you run and a share of crops or livestock from land you let a farmer use'), scope.rent_personal (a fishing vessel rented out is something other than a building, room or land), royalty.business (royalty from an oil or gas working interest or the filer's own writing is refused), and sche.qbi_business (a rental treated as a trade or business for QBI is refused, so a rental never carries QBI). Without a Schedule C the tool has no qualified business, so a suspended loss cannot change Form 8995. One real gap: look-back interest is owed for the year a contract is completed or adjusted (i6251 p. 7), and s2.lookback asks only about a contract finished in 2025.

findings.evidence: i8995 p. 4, Line 3, quoted correctly. Without a Schedule C the tool has no QBI business: a K-1 is refused by scope.k1, a farm by scope.farm, a rental treated as a trade or business by sche.qbi_business (forms/2025/sche.yaml refuses), and qbi.yaml's note limits QBI to Schedule C businesses and section 199A dividends. A loss of a closed sole proprietorship allowed in 2025 is deducted on a 2025 Schedule C, which makes s1.has_sc true; a passive one is screened by scope.passive behind scope.business_before.

i1040gi p. 93, Line 16 'If you were self-employed or a partner', quoted correctly. A partner is refused by scope.k1 and a Schedule F farmer by scope.farm before the business section, so only a Schedule C filer reaches scope.se_plan_other.

The cited Line 16 condition is wider than the gate, but the part outside it (partners, farmers) is refused by scope.k1 and scope.farm; the gate's Schedule C condition is the remaining in-scope part. No defect.

i6251 p. 7, Lines 2o, 2q, 2t, quoted correctly. A pass-through's IDCs, mining or circulation costs come on a Schedule K-1 (scope.k1 refuses); an oil or gas working interest held directly is refused on Schedule E by royalty.business ('from an oil or gas working interest'), and depletion by royalty.depletion and rental.depletion.

f1040s2 line 17n, quoted correctly. A partner's look-back interest comes through a K-1 (scope.k1 refuses). An author's income-forecast property is refused through royalty.business ('own work as a self-employed writer'). A passive investor in film rights reporting royalties on Schedule E with forecast depreciation remains possible but very rare; noted with BUG-0821, not a separate defect.

i1040sj p. 1, quoted correctly. Fishing through a partnership is refused by scope.k1; leasing a fishing vessel is rental of something other than a building, room or land, refused by scope.rent_personal. Schedule J is also an election ('This is a choice ... to go on without it, answer No'), so a No yields a correct return without averaging.

i6251 p. 7, Line 2p: 'you may owe or be entitled to a refund of interest for the tax year the contract is completed or adjusted', checked. s2.lookback asks 'Did you ... finish a contract in 2025 that ran over more than one tax year'; a contract finished earlier and adjusted in 2025 is a truthful No, and line 17n is dropped instead of refused. Rare (small contracts are often exempt). Low.

unruled:gate:s1.hobby_any#1.class: defect (medium): 'make money' reads as net profit, so a hobby run at a loss drops its receipts (BUG-0822)
unruled:gate:s1.hobby_any#1.reason: Line 8j takes gross receipts (p525 p. 31; the amount help says costs are not subtracted), but the gate asks whether the filer 'made money', which a filer whose hobby lost money reads as No. A recreational farm is refused by scope.farm ('income or a loss from farming'), and an activity the filer runs as a business reaches Schedule C, where sc.special lists 'an activity that is not a business (for example a sporadic activity, a not-for-profit activity or a hobby)'.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 31, 'You must include on your return income from an activity, even if you don't expect to make a profit from that activity ... line 8j', checked. s1.hobby_any: 'make money from a hobby or pastime'; s1.hobby_income help: 'the costs of a hobby are not subtracted'. A loss-making hobby is a plausible No and its receipts are dropped. Medium.

p525 p. 31, 'a farm you operate mostly for recreation and pleasure', checked. scope.farm asks 'income or a loss from farming?' of every filer and a Yes ends the interview, so a recreational farm never reaches line 8j.

A filer who treats the activity as a business reports it on Schedule C, so the receipts are not dropped; sc.special then asks about 'an activity that is not a business (for example a sporadic activity, a not-for-profit activity or a hobby)', which refuses it.
p525 p. 31 refers to income generally. 'Make money' may be read as cash only, so barter or goods received from a hobby are dropped. Same rewording (BUG-0822); low on its own.

unruled:gate:s1.inmate_wages#1.class: low defect: 'while in a jail or prison' misses work release and other correctional facilities (BUG-0823)
unruled:gate:s1.inmate_wages#1.reason: Line 8u takes pay for services performed while an inmate in a penal institution (i1040gi p. 92), a status test; the gate asks about work done 'while in a jail or prison', a place test with a narrower facility word.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8u, 'services performed while an inmate in a penal institution', checked; p. 23, Line 1a says such wages are not on line 1a. s1.inmate_wages: 'paid for work done while in a jail or prison?'. A work-release inmate can read this as work inside the facility and answer No; 1099 pay is dropped, W-2 pay stays on line 1a as EIC earned income (p596: inmate earnings 'aren't earned income'). Rare; low.
'Penal institution' (i1040gi p. 92) is wider than 'jail or prison' (camps, detention or reentry centers). Same rewording; low.

unruled:gate:s1.jury_any#1.class: low defect: 'paid for serving on a jury' can exclude jury-pool fees (BUG-0824)
unruled:gate:s1.jury_any#1.reason: Line 8h takes any jury duty pay (i1040gi p. 91; p525 p. 34); a juror paid for jury-selection days but never seated may answer No to 'serving on a jury'.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 91, Line 8h 'Enter any jury duty pay', and p525 p. 34, checked. s1.jury_any: 'were you ... paid for serving on a jury?' A pool juror dismissed in voir dire can read this as No and the attendance fees are dropped. Small amounts; low.

unruled:gate:s1.scholarship_any#1.class: low defect: 'a grant for study' can read as excluding a research fellowship (BUG-0825); the WIDE findings are accepted
unruled:gate:s1.scholarship_any#1.reason: Line 8r takes scholarship and fellowship grants not on a W-2, the whole amount for a non-degree candidate (i1040gi p. 92). The gate's trailing 'for study' and its Pell-grant help can lead a research fellow to answer No. The two WIDE cases are answered by the amount question (s1.scholarship_taxable) with zero.
