findings.evidence: Any Schedule K-1 (partnership, S corporation, estate or trust) is a Yes to scope.k1 ('A Yes ends the interview here'), refused through scope.schedule1; a K-3 is refused too (k1p.r_b16, k1s.box14). The entity-level case never reaches this question.

Any Schedule K-1 (partnership, S corporation, estate or trust) is a Yes to scope.k1 ('A Yes ends the interview here'), refused through scope.schedule1; a K-3 is refused too (k1p.r_b16, k1s.box14). The entity-level case never reaches this question.
i1116 p. 3. Tax withheld at source read as not 'paid': as the earlier ruling of gate:ftc.carryover_ask (BUG-0620). Foreign royalties and rents are refused on Form 1116 by f1116.rental.
Opens the gate with nothing to enter; extra questions only.

unruled:gate:ftc.carryover_if_asked#1.reason: A carryover reduced to zero before 2025 leaves no carryover to use; the Schedule B lines it would show cancel.

findings.evidence: i1116sb pp. 1-2. With the 2024 carryover wiped out, line 3 is zero either way; only the Schedule B lines 1 and 2 that cancel are not printed. A carryover created by a smaller actual carryback is a different case: BUG-0834 item 2.

unruled:gate:ftc.has_tax#1.class: no gate defect: the deduction is not prepared; K-1 refused; territories asked
unruled:gate:ftc.has_tax#1.reason: The foreign tax deduction is outside the tool (elective, and refused when chosen); pass-through tax comes with a refused K-1; the trigger question names U.S. territory income.

findings.evidence: i1116 p. 2. A deduction of non-creditable foreign tax is elective; the tool does not prepare a foreign tax deduction (sa.foreign_tax_deduct's help: 'This tool does not figure the deduction; to go on without it, answer No'), and a Yes refuses (sa.unsupported). Leaving it out does not understate tax.

Any Schedule K-1 (partnership, S corporation, estate or trust) is a Yes to scope.k1 ('A Yes ends the interview here'), refused through scope.schedule1; a K-3 is refused too (k1p.r_b16, k1s.box14). The entity-level case never reaches this question.

The reviewer saw the label ('another country'). The question as asked, s3.foreign_any, is 'Have you ... ever paid income tax to another country, had income from a U.S. territory, or owned 10% or more of a foreign company?', so a filer with territory income answers Yes.
Extra questions only.

unruled:gate:sb.bonds_any_if_income#1.class: defect (low): the help excludes certificates of deposit
unruled:gate:sb.bonds_any_if_income#1.reason: Nominee income has its own question; the CD exclusion is BUG-0832; the rest covered or wide.

findings.evidence: i1040sb p. 1. sb.nominee is asked of every filer with income (sb.nominee_if_income), separately from this gate, and sets sb.unsupported.
The gate cites the Schedule B list, of which the nominee item is asked by sb.nominee; the citation is wider than this gate's condition. No amount.
i1040sb p. 2. f1040.tax_exempt_interest's help says 'less any bond premium', so line 2a is net.
Bonds in a brokerage account are owned directly, not through a fund; the help says 'If you are not sure, answer Yes'.
i1040sb p. 2, OID Adjustment. sb.bonds_any's help 'Interest from ... a certificate of deposit ... is not what this asks about' turns away a CD holder with an OID or premium adjustment.
One extra question. Safe.
Seller financing to a non-resident buyer draws Yes; refusal only. Safe.

unruled:gate:sb.foreign_any#1.class: defect (low): the gates miss indirect financial interests
unruled:gate:sb.foreign_any#1.reason: Findings 0 and 1 are BUG-0831 item 1; Form 8814 is refused; the help covers 3 and 4.

findings.evidence: fincen114 p. 5. An account of a U.S. entity the filer owns more than half of is named only in sb.line7a's help, after the gate.
i8938 p. 8. Assets of a disregarded entity or grantor trust are not named in sb.asset_any.
Form 8814 is refused for every filer: scope.f8814, through scope.other_line16.
sb.asset_any's help: 'shares of a foreign company not held in a U.S. brokerage account'.
sb.asset_any's help: 'a share of an estate abroad, even if nothing has been paid yet'.
Territory accounts open the gate with nothing to report. Extra questions only.

unruled:gate:sb.foreign_company_any#1.class: defect (low): votes and indirect holdings are not named
unruled:gate:sb.foreign_company_any#1.reason: Both UNCLEAR are BUG-0831 item 3; the WIDE items are safe.

findings.evidence: i1040sb p. 2, '(b) combined voting power'. sb.company_any does not say value or votes.
Shares held through entities or options count in sb.form5471's help, not in the gate.
Territory items open the gate. Extra questions only.
A foreign entity that is not a corporation opens the gate. Extra questions only.

unruled:gate:sb.foreign_trust_any#1.class: defect (low): the trust gate is narrower than line 8

findings.evidence: cfr-26-301-7701-7 p. 4, control test. The gate tests location and trustee residence only.
i1040sb p. 3. A sale or loan to the trust, or a loan or free use received from it, is not 'gave to it' or 'may receive from it'; sb.line8 names them.
f1040sb line 8. The present tense misses a connection that ended in 2025.
Receipt through an intermediary is named only in sb.line8's help.
Territory items open the gate. Extra question only.

unruled:gate:sd.sold_other#1.class: defect (low): mineral property is not named in the gate
unruled:gate:sd.sold_other#1.reason: The 1244 stock, condemnation and trader cases have their own ungated questions; mineral property is BUG-0835.

findings.evidence: i1040sd p. 1, item 1c. Named only in sd.business_property, behind the gate.
sd.small_business_stock is asked of every filer (not behind this gate) and refuses through sd.other_forms.
sd.condemned is asked of every filer and refuses through sd.other_forms.
sd.trader_election is asked of every filer and refuses through sd.other_forms.
Section 126 property is farm property, refused by scope.farm; other noncapital business assets are 'anything you used in a business' in the help.
A home sold for cash draws Yes and one more question. Safe.

unruled:f8853c.nonqualified#1.class: no gate defect; the box 4 test is the issuer's report of the status
unruled:f8853c.nonqualified#1.reason: The question asks about box 4 of Form 1099-LTC; a box that contradicts the contract is an issuer error, and a Yes on a qualified contract only refuses.

findings.evidence: i8853 p. 8 defines a qualified contract (post-1996 under 7702B, or pre-1997 meeting state law and not materially changed); box 4 of Form 1099-LTC is the issuer's statement of that status, and the help says most policies are checked. A grandfathered contract is qualified and should be checked; a filer reading an unchecked box answers Yes and is refused at f8853c.line26 (safe). The reverse (a nonqualified contract reported as qualified) rests on a wrong information return, which no question can catch.

unruled:f8853c.others_paid#1.reason: The interview asks only about others paid at a set rate, which is the Multiple Payees condition; an assignee reading refuses, safe.

findings.evidence: The interview prompt is 'was anyone besides you ... also paid at a set rate under a policy on this person?', so a lump-sum accelerated death benefit to another person is answered No, as i8853 p. 8-9 (Line 15 and Multiple Payees: the aggregate covers 'all persons who received per diem payments ... or as accelerated death benefits because the insured was chronically ill') allows. The finding read the encoding's source wording. Note: BUG-0873 proposes naming any accelerated death benefit to another person; this finding argues against that part of its fix.

i8853 p. 8, 'The policyholder is required to report the income, even if payment is assigned to a third party'. A filer who counts the nursing home receiving assigned payments answers Yes and is refused at f8853c.line26. Safe.

unruled:f8853c.contract_before_ltc_date#.class: no gate defect; WIDE by design
unruled:f8853c.contract_before_ltc_date#.reason: A modified pre-1996 contract is refused though line 24 would be right; the refusal remedy names that case. The scope of 'that' errs safe either way.

findings.evidence: i8853 p. 9, Line 24 Caution, 'you must include reimbursements if the contract was exchanged or modified after July 31, 1996'. The Yes refuses at f8853c.line25, whose remedy says 'unless the contract was later changed; that is outside this tool'. Safe.

The line 24 question does not tell the filer to leave pre-1996 reimbursements out, so line 24 holds all reimbursements and a Yes refuses (safe). A filer who left them out under the general rule (i8853 p. 9, 'Generally, don't include on line 24') and answers No has line 25 as the instruction figures it. Either reading is safe; the wording is reworded under BUG-0873.

unruled:f8853c.rate_changed#1.reason: The interview asks whether a policy started or stopped paying partway through, which catches the stop-and-restart case; the other two readings refuse, safe.

findings.evidence: The interview prompt is 'did the rate of those payments change, or did a policy start or stop paying partway through?'. A contract that stops in May and resumes in September stopped paying partway through: Yes, refused at f8853c.line26 (the more-than-one-LTC-period refusal, i8853 p. 8, Line 18).
i8853 p. 9, Method 2: two contracts paying from March 1 through December 31 make one LTC period. A filer who reads 'start ... partway through' as covering both answers Yes and is refused. Safe.
i8853 p. 9: a contract paying $1,500 per month has one rate. A filer who computes a varying daily figure and answers Yes is refused. Safe; unlikely given 'daily, weekly or monthly rate'.

unruled:f8889.former_spouse_family#1.class: defect (wording): legal separation not named; one WIDE
unruled:f8889.former_spouse_family#1.reason: The spouse-not-eligible case refuses, safe. A marriage ended by a decree of separate maintenance is not named; filed with the false-no lane's entry.

findings.evidence: i8889 p. 4: the family rule needs both spouses eligible; a then-spouse not eligible still draws a Yes and a refusal at f8889.line13_figured. Safe.

The prompt names only 'divorce or death'; a marriage ended in 2025 by a decree of separate maintenance (not married for the year under the household rules) may be answered No and the then-spouse's family months are counted self-only (line 3 limit understated). Annulment is not a marriage, so No is right there. Recorded in BUG-0874 (its fix names a decree of separate maintenance). Low.

unruled:ira.deduct_less#1.reason: The prompt compares with the most the rules allow, so a capped deduction is not a smaller one; a zero deduction is deducting less.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 98, line 12. The prompt is 'Do you want to deduct less ... than the most the rules allow', and the help says almost everyone answers No. A filer who misreads answers Yes and is refused at ira.less_gate. Safe.
Electing no deduction is deducting less than the most allowed; the prompt's 'deduct less ... and treat the rest as not deducted' covers it, and the Yes refuses at ira.less_gate (p590a p. 16).

unruled:ssb.lump_elect#1.reason: Wanting the election with nothing taxable refuses a case the worksheet computes. Safe.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 31, Line 6c: the election helps only when benefits are taxable. A Yes refuses at ssb.lump_sum though line 6b would be zero. Safe.

unruled:gate:f8853c.has_line24#1.reason: The 'paid back' wording of the line 24 and pre-1996 questions is the false-no lane's BUG-0873; the modified-contract case refuses, safe.

findings.evidence: i8853 p. 9, Line 24 and its Caution. The line 24 question does not ask the filer to leave pre-1996 amounts out, so line 24 holds them and the pre-1996 question is reached; its 'paid back' wording (and line 24's 'paid back to you') is narrower than 'received or expect to receive, through insurance or otherwise'. Recorded in BUG-0873, medium.
i8853 p. 9, Line 24 Caution: a contract modified after July 31, 1996 belongs on line 24; the Yes refuses at f8853c.line25, whose remedy names the case. Safe.

unruled:gate:f8853c.has_periodic#1.reason: (0) the 'paid back to you' wording of line 24 is BUG-0873 (unfixed: the prompt is unchanged); (1) asking line 22 when line 21 controls costs a question; (2) a Method 1 filer whose rate changed is refused, safe.

findings.evidence: i8853 p. 9, Line 24, 'Enter the reimbursements you received or expect to receive through insurance or otherwise'. The interview still asks 'How much of those care costs was paid back to you, by insurance or otherwise?' (help 'Count insurance or other payments that repaid those costs'); an expected reimbursement or one paid to the provider can be left out, understating line 24 and line 26. Recorded in BUG-0873, medium.
f8853 line 23, 'Enter the larger of line 21 or line 22'. f8853c.line22 is asked whenever line 20 is positive; when line 21 is larger the answer changes nothing. One extra question; safe.

i8853 p. 8, Method 1, 'your LTC period is the same period as that used by the insurance company'. f8853c.rate_changed refuses any rate change (f8853c.line26), which is needed under Method 2 and over-inclusive under Method 1. A wrong refusal, not a missed amount; safe.

unruled:gate:f8853c.periodic#1.class: defect (wording) recorded for weekly or other periods; the rest covered or outside the tool
unruled:gate:f8853c.periodic#1.reason: 'Per day or month' omits other periods (BUG-0873); accelerated death benefits are named in the opening tick; a wrong box 3 is an issuer error.

findings.evidence: i8853 p. 8, Per Diem Payments: 'payments of a fixed amount made on a periodic basis'. The interview says 'a set amount per day or month' while the encoding says 'per day, week or month'; the box 3 mark named in the question limits the risk. Recorded in BUG-0873.

The opening tick of this collection is 'A long-term care insurance payout, or life insurance paid early, in 2025' and its help names Form 1099-LTC; the per diem mark in box 3 of Form 1099-LTC applies to box 2 accelerated death benefits as well (i8853 p. 8, Line 19), and line 19 asks 'How much life insurance was paid early, at a set rate'.

i8853 p. 8: box 3 'should indicate' per diem. The question leads with the substance ('a set amount ... whatever the care cost') and gives the box as its mark; a box 3 that contradicts the payment terms is a wrong information return.

unruled:gate:f8889.ask_former_spouse_fam.reason: The 'while' and divorce-or-death wording is the false-no lane's BUG-0874; the not-eligible spouse refuses, safe.

findings.evidence: i8889 p. 4, How To Complete Part I (month by month). The prompt 'Did a marriage of yours end ... while the other person had' reads as coverage at the end; a then-spouse whose family plan ended before the divorce is answered No and the line 3 limit is understated. BUG-0874, low.
The prompt names only divorce or death; a decree of separate maintenance is not named. BUG-0874, low.
i8889 p. 4: the rule needs both spouses eligible; a then-spouse not eligible still draws a Yes and a refusal at f8889.line13_figured. Safe.

unruled:gate:f8889.inherited_any#1.reason: The account beneficiary's own final return is asked at f8889.owner_died; the earlier-year non-spouse case costs a question.

findings.evidence: i8889 p. 3, 'If the account beneficiary's estate is the beneficiary, the value of the HSA as of the date of death is included on the account beneficiary's final income tax return'. f8889.owner_died asks whether the person this Form 8889 is for died in 2025, and its wording includes an HSA whose beneficiary is the estate; it refuses. f8889.inherited_any is about someone else's HSA.
A non-spouse beneficiary of an earlier-year death answers Yes and picks 'Someone else, earlier year' in f8889.inherited_case, which refuses nothing. An extra question.

unruled:gate:f8889.mfs_ask#1.class: defect (wording) recorded for the present tense; the rest covered or presentation
unruled:gate:f8889.mfs_ask#1.reason: Joint returns split the family limit through the allocation lines; the present-tense spouse-HSA question is the false-no lane's BUG-0874.

findings.evidence: i8889 p. 7, Line 6. On a joint return the separate-HSA split is figured by the allocation lines (f8889.allocation, f8889.line6_split, person.hsa_share); the separate-return question is needed only because the spouse's side is not on this return.

The prompt 'Does your husband or wife have a health savings account' is present tense while the line (and i8889 p. 7, 'Spouses who have separate HSAs and had family coverage ... at any time during 2025') concern 2025; a spouse's HSA closed after taking 2025 contributions is answered No. BUG-0874, low.
The f8889 collection frame 'For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return)' precedes a question asked only on a separate return; 'your husband or wife' still names the person. Wording only.

unruled:gate:f8889.testing_failed_figure.reason: A 2025 transfer refuses at f8889.ira_transfer; the filer-facing questions carry no timing ambiguity; the wrong disability No and the WIDE cases refuse, safe.

findings.evidence: A qualified HSA funding distribution made in 2025 is refused at f8889.line13_figured / line13_none through f8889.ira_transfer ('Was any money moved into your HSA straight from an IRA in 2025?'), so its testing period is never figured.

The filer sees f8889.ira_gap ('From the month of that transfer until 12 months after it, was there a month in which you could not have an HSA?'), not the helper's label; the months asked include 2025.

i8889 p. 2, 'other than because of death or becoming disabled'. A filer who reads 'stop being able to have an HSA' as closing the account answers No to f8889.disabled and is refused at f8889.testing_failed. Safe.

i8889 p. 8, testing period through the 12th month. f8889.ira_gap asks only the months of the testing period, so a loss of eligibility after it ends does not refuse through the transfer; any refusal through the last-month rule is safe.
i8889 p. 2: death also excuses the failure; the refusal is wider. Safe; the return of a person who died is rare here.

unruled:gate:retirement.cost_any_if_plan.reason: The death benefit exclusion is asked of a plan beneficiary at retirement.death_exclusion and refused; full recovery costs questions.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 29, Simplified Method Worksheet, Before you begin (death benefit exclusion up to $5,000 for a death before August 21, 1996). A code 4 plan distribution asks retirement.death_exclusion (gated by retirement.plan_death), and a Yes refuses. The help of retirement.cost_any also says 'If you are not sure, answer Yes'. The 'former employee' wording of that question is BUG-0875.
i1040gi p. 28: payments are fully taxable once the cost is recovered; the extra Simplified Method questions change nothing. Safe.

unruled:gate:retirement.disability_if_pl.reason: Forms 1099-R are listed per person, so 'you' is the recipient; the plan-without-disability-provision case asks extra questions here (its amount effect is completeness item retirement#1.1).

findings.evidence: The retirement collection is asked per person: 'For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return) — ... List each Form 1099-R you received'. A spouse's pension is listed under the spouse, and 'you' in its questions is the spouse.

i1040gi p. 30. The gate holds and the gated questions are asked; that alone costs questions. Whether a Yes then moves such payments to line 1h is the completeness claim retirement#1.1, filed as BUG-0878.

unruled:gate:retirement.is_code7#1.reason: Codes 1, J and S over 59 1/2 are handled by exception 12 in retirement.exception; the code-7 gate looks for a code that does not fit; the recipient is the listed person.

findings.evidence: i5329 p. 5, Exception 12. A code 1 distribution goes to retirement.exception, whose list includes '12 incorrectly coded as early' (Enum early_exception, e01 to e23); the age at receipt sets that amount there, not at the code 7 gate.

The gate's purpose is the reverse case: code 7 under 59 1/2 is a code that does not fit and refuses at retirement.code_screen unless a section 457 plan. Its citation is the generic line 2 sentence; no amount depends on it.
Forms 1099-R are listed per person ('For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return) — ... List each Form 1099-R you received'), so 'you' is the recipient.
A code 7 distribution received after 59 1/2 is asked the age question; one extra question.

unruled:gate:retirement.is_ira#1.reason: The model read the gate's polarity backwards: each plan-only line asks its question when retirement.is_ira is false.

findings.evidence: retirement.born_before_averaging_date_if_plan chooses retirement.born_before_averaging_date when retirement.is_ira is false (a plan) and false only for an IRA. The Form 4972 question is asked of plan distributions (i1040gi p. 30).
retirement.pso_exclusion_if_plan asks retirement.pso_exclusion when retirement.is_ira is false (i1040gi p. 28).
retirement.cost_any_if_plan asks retirement.cost_any when retirement.is_ira is false; cost recovery is asked of pensions (i1040gi pp. 28, 30).
retirement.disability_if_plan asks retirement.disability when retirement.is_ira is false (i1040gi p. 28).
retirement.box6_if_plan and retirement.loan_offset_if_plan ask their questions when retirement.is_ira is false.
The gate is used in both polarities: true selects the IRA-only lines, false the plan-only lines; no line is inverted.

unruled:gate:retirement.is_trad#1.reason: IRA basis is asked of the person who lists the form; 2025 nondeductible contributions with a distribution refuse at f8606.line14; any earlier Form 8606 refusing is safe.

findings.evidence: Forms 1099-R are listed per person, so 'you' in retirement.ira_basis is the IRA owner who received the distribution (i1040gi p. 27, Exception 2(1)).

A 2025 nondeductible contribution with a 2025 traditional IRA distribution is refused at f8606.line14 through f8606.dist ('With nondeductible contributions and a 2025 distribution from a traditional IRA ... Form 8606 lines 4 to 13, which this tool does not prepare').
The help says any earlier Form 8606 means Yes; a Roth-only Form 8606 refuses a case with no basis. Safe.

unruled:gate:retirement.plan_death#1.class: defect (wording): the beneficiary questions name only an employee who died before retiring
unruled:gate:retirement.plan_death#1.reason: retirement.ben_before_retire's '(before retiring)' and retirement.death_exclusion's 'the employee' are narrower than i1040gi; filed low.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 30, 'If you are the survivor of a retiree, use the retiree's age on their annuity starting date ... If you are the beneficiary of an employee who died, see Pub. 575.' The parenthetical '(before retiring)' can lead the beneficiary of a person who retired but died before the annuity starting date to answer No and skip the refusal. BUG-0875, low.

i1040gi p. 29, 'deceased employee or former employee who died before August 21, 1996'. retirement.death_exclusion asks about 'the employee'; a retiree's beneficiary may answer No and the exclusion is neither applied nor refused (taxable amount overstated). BUG-0875, low.

unruled:gate:retirement.put_back#1.reason: retirement.rollover_any names conversions and does not say 'another' account; the WIDE finding costs questions.

findings.evidence: The filer sees retirement.rollover_any, 'Did any of this money go into a retirement account again (a rollover or a conversion), even if it was paid to you first?', with help 'Money moved into a Roth IRA counts'; a conversion is Yes and retirement.roth_moved refuses it (i1040gi p. 27, Exception 2).
The same question says 'a retirement account again', not 'another'; a redeposit into the same IRA is Yes (i1040gi p. 30, Rollovers).
An ordinary rollover is asked the four refusal questions; extra questions only.

unruled:gate:retirement.under59_if_code7.reason: A section 457 distribution coded 1 takes exception 13 in retirement.exception; the recipient is the listed person.

findings.evidence: i5329 p. 5, Exception 13. A code 1 distribution goes to retirement.exception, whose list (e01 to e23) includes 13, the section 457 exception; the code 7 gate concerns only a code 7 under 59 1/2.
Forms 1099-R are listed per person, so 'you' in retirement.under59 is the person who received the distribution.

unruled:gate:sli.any_if_not_mfs#1.class: defect (wording): a loan not named a student loan; one WIDE
unruled:gate:sli.any_if_not_mfs#1.reason: The tick turns on the loan's name; the help covers doubt but not a filer sure a personal loan is not a student loan. Filed low.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 98, Line 21: a qualified student loan is any loan taken out to pay qualified higher education expenses. The tick 'Paid interest on a student loan' leads a filer whose personal loan or credit line paid only school costs to answer No, dropping deductible interest. BUG-0876, low.
i1040gi p. 99: unqualified loans give no deduction; the questions beneath sort them out (sli.unqualified_any). Extra questions only.

unruled:gate:ssb.any#1.reason: A repayment-only filer is asked at s3.repaid_income, whose help names social security repayments, and refused.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 31, Repayments: a deduction or credit only when repayments exceed benefits by more than $3,000. s3.repaid_income asks about paying back more than $3,000 and its help says 'For social security benefits, count only what you paid back above the benefits you received in 2025'; a Yes refuses (Schedule 3 line 13b / Schedule A line 16). A repayment of $3,000 or less gives nothing, and line 6a is zero either way.

unruled:gate:ssb.prior_year_pay#1.reason: A missed Yes only skips an election this tool refuses; the return without the election is a correct return. The WIDE finding costs a question.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 31, Line 6c: the lump-sum election is optional ('you may be able to reduce'). A Yes here leads only to ssb.lump_elect, whose Yes refuses; an RRB-1099 recipient who answers No gets a correct return without the election.
With nothing taxable the election question is still asked; one extra question.
